primary.title: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica
primary.author: Isaac Newton
primary.rationale: Newton's seminal work laying out the laws of motion and universal gravitation. It is a foundational text in physics and mathematics.

primary.title: Opticks
primary.author: Isaac Newton
primary.rationale: A major work detailing Newton's experiments and theories on light and color, including his development of the reflecting telescope.

primary.title: The Chronology of Ancient Kingdoms Amended
primary.author: Isaac Newton
primary.rationale: Published posthumously, this work reflects Newton's extensive studies in history and chronology, applying mathematical principles to historical timelines.

secondary.title: Principia: The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy
secondary.author: Isaac Newton
secondary.rationale: A modern translation and scholarly analysis of Newton's Principia Mathematica, providing context and interpretation for his groundbreaking work.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Newton
secondary.author: Isaac Newton
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Newton's life, work, and influence, offering a comprehensive overview.

secondary.title: Isaac Newton
secondary.author: James Gleick
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded biography that explores Newton's scientific achievements, personal life, and intellectual context, written for a broad audience but based on scholarly research.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are foundational texts. Secondary sources provide scholarly analysis and biographical context from reputable authors and publishers.
